questions.prompt: How can multipart/alternative structure be abused?
options: The message carries both plain-text and HTML versions, so benign text can occupy the plain part while the payload sits in the HTML the user actually sees
questions.explanation: Tooling that samples the plain-text part sees something harmless while the rendered HTML delivers the actual attack.

questions.prompt: What does a right-to-left override character (U+202E) accomplish in a filename?
options: It reverses the displayed filename so an executable can appear to have a document extension, while the actual extension is unchanged
It hides the file from Explorer entirely
questions.explanation: The rendering is reversed but the file itself is not -- invoice[U+202E]fdp.exe displays as invoiceexe.pdf while remaining an executable.

questions.prompt: Why did ISO and VHD attachments become a common delivery method?
options: They historically did not propagate Mark of the Web to their contents, stripping the mark that causes Office to block macros
They cannot be scanned by mail gateways
questions.explanation: Removing MOTW restores macro execution in delivered documents, which made container formats a direct answer to a specific defensive control.

questions.prompt: Why does an OST file matter when server-side mailbox data is gone?
options: OST files are stored on the mail server
The OST is the local cached copy on the endpoint, and may be the only surviving record of what the mailbox contained
OST files cannot be parsed forensically
OST files contain only calendar data
questions.explanation: When a mailbox has been wiped server-side, the endpoint's cached copy -- parseable with libpff -- can preserve the content that no longer exists anywhere else.
